Procedure (verified 2026-06-29 with `c7daa85 chore: ignore llm-wiki`): (1) `git checkout -b tmp <github-sha>` then `git cherry-pick <tangled-unique-sha>` → new commit `X` = GitHub + the work; (2) verify `git diff <github-sha> X` shows *only* the intended delta; (3) push `X` to GitHub main — it's a clean fast-forward from the old GitHub head (`git push <github-url> HEAD:main`), no force, so branch protection that allows FF accepts it; (4) force-push `X` to tangled, replacing the old tangled commit: `git push --force-with-lease=main:<old-tangled-sha> <tangled-url> HEAD:main` (content preserved — the cherry-pick carries it); (5) realign the **main checkout's local `main`** — it still points at the now-superseded direct commit (`<tangled-unique-sha>`), which is a strict *subset* of `X`, so `git reset --hard X` on a clean tree loses nothing (old SHA stays in reflog); (6) `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main X` in the worktree to kill the phantom-divergence (see gotcha below), then `just sync-tangled-main` → "✓ already in sync". The cherry-pick gives the work a NEW SHA, so the original tangled commit can never be an ancestor of GitHub — a force-push to tangled is unavoidable, but it's safe because the content is preserved on GitHub.
26	
27	**Gotcha — `--force-with-lease` to a bare URL fails with "stale info":** the bare lease compares against the remote-*tracking* ref (`refs/remotes/origin/main`), but a push to a URL (not the named remote) has no tracking ref to lease against, so git rejects blind. Fix: pass the explicit expected value — `git push --force-with-lease=main:<current-tangled-sha> git@knot.malpercio.dev:malpercio.dev/ezpds main`. (`<current-tangled-sha>` = what `origin/main` / `FETCH_HEAD` says tangled is now.) If it STILL says stale info with the explicit SHA, tangled genuinely moved — stop and re-check.
28	
29	**Gotcha — after a URL push, `git status` shows phantom "diverged" forever:** pushing to a URL and the recipe's `git fetch <url> main` (lands in `FETCH_HEAD`) never update `refs/remotes/origin/main`, so the cached ref stays at the old SHA and git keeps reporting divergence even though the remotes match. Fix: `git fetch origin` (canonical), or — if you've already proven the remote's SHA via `FETCH_HEAD` — `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main <sha>` (instant, no network).
30	
31	**Gotcha:** the shell here is **zsh**, where `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is empty — to capture a piped command's real exit, wrap in `bash -c '... | tail; echo EXIT=${PIPESTATUS[0]}'`, else the harness reports the trailing echo's exit, not the command's. 12	Biggest **safe** reclaim: stale per-worktree `target/` dirs under `.claude/worktrees/*/target` (each multi-GB; one was 21 GB). 14	**Bigger lever (confirmed 2026-06-29, reclaimed ~60 GB from a 100%-full disk):** when a worktree's branch is already merged into `main`, remove the *whole* worktree, not just its `target/`. 16	Two gotchas hit that run:
17	- **Sandbox blocks `.devenv` deletion**: `rm`/`git worktree remove` on trees containing `.devenv` fails with `Operation not permitted` (EPERM) even though files have normal perms, no `uchg` flag, and a writable parent. That's the command-sandbox fingerprint (vs. EACCES for real perms) → retry with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`. Source-only worktrees (no `.devenv`) delete fine in-sandbox.
18	- **`git worktree remove` unregisters *before* deleting files**, so if the file delete fails (sandbox), it orphans the dir on disk while dropping it from `git worktree list`. Recover with plain `rm -rf .claude/worktrees/<name>` (sandbox off) then `git worktree prune`.
